categories.name: Coding Agents
categories.description: AI-powered tools that write, review, and debug code directly in your development workflow.

categories.name: Research Agents
categories.description: AI agents specialized in finding, synthesizing, and analyzing information from various sources.

categories.name: General / Personal Agents
categories.description: Versatile AI assistants for everyday tasks including writing, analysis, brainstorming, and conversation.

categories.name: Creative Agents
categories.description: AI tools for generating images, music, video, and other creative media.

categories.name: Frameworks & Platforms
categories.description: Developer tools and SDKs for building custom AI agents and multi-agent workflows.

agents.name: Muse Code
agents.description: A terminal coding agent for macOS and Linux, released August 5, 2026 and co-trained as one unit with Muse Spark 1.2 so the model and the harness share goals, compaction, and subagent recipes. Runs persistent background agents across a session and keeps a replay-safe event log so it survives a crash.
agents.pricing: Usage-based via the Meta Model API: $1.25/$4.25 per 1M tokens standard, or $0.10/$0.20 on the contributor tier if you let Meta train on your data

agents.name: DeepSeek Harness
agents.description: A plugin-first open-source coding agent released August 13, 2026 under MIT, aimed directly at Claude Code. Shipped the same day DeepSeek moved V4-Pro to general availability and raised API prices, pairing an open harness with a more expensive model.
agents.pricing: Free and open source under MIT; model inference billed separately

agents.name: Grok Build
agents.description: xAI's official terminal coding agent, invoked as the grok command. Runs up to 8 parallel sub-agents and has defaulted to Grok 4.6 with a 500K context window since August 12, 2026.
agents.pricing: No standalone plan; bundled into xAI subscriptions at SuperGrok $30/mo, X Premium+ $40/mo, and SuperGrok Heavy $300/mo. Every tier unlocks the same CLI and differs only in usage limits. Headless use via the API bills grok-build-0.1 at roughly $0.20/$1.50 per 1M tokens

agents.name: Claude Code
agents.description: An agentic CLI tool that lets Claude operate directly in your terminal, reading files, editing code, running commands, and managing git workflows autonomously.
agents.pricing: Usage-based via Claude API

agents.name: Cursor
agents.description: An AI-native code editor built on VS Code that provides inline code generation, multi-file editing, and codebase-aware chat powered by multiple foundation models. SpaceX closed its $60 billion all-stock acquisition of maker Anysphere on August 14, 2026, folding Cursor into the SpaceXAI unit alongside Grok Build and Grok Bot.
agents.pricing: Free tier, Pro $20/mo, Business $40/mo

agents.name: GitHub Copilot
agents.description: An AI pair programmer integrated into popular editors that suggests code completions, generates functions from comments, and offers chat-based coding assistance.
agents.pricing: Individual $10/mo, Business $19/mo, Enterprise $39/mo

agents.name: Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf)
agents.description: An AI-native developer environment (rebranded from Windsurf in June 2026) that provides a unified surface for managing local and cloud coding agents, including Devin, Claude Code, Codex, and custom agents through the Agent Client Protocol.
agents.pricing: Free tier, Pro $15/mo, Teams $30/mo

agents.name: Perplexity
agents.description: An AI-powered answer engine that searches the web in real time, synthesizes information from multiple sources, and provides cited responses to complex questions.
agents.pricing: Free tier, Pro $20/mo

agents.name: Elicit
agents.description: A research assistant that helps find and analyze academic papers, extract key claims, and summarize findings across large bodies of scientific literature.
agents.pricing: Free tier, Plus $10/mo, Enterprise custom

agents.name: Consensus
agents.description: A search engine that uses AI to find and synthesize results from peer-reviewed scientific research, providing evidence-based answers with citations.
agents.pricing: Free tier, Premium $9.99/mo

agents.name: ChatGPT
agents.description: A general-purpose AI assistant that can handle conversation, writing, coding, analysis, and web browsing, with plugin and custom GPT support for specialized tasks.
agents.pricing: Free tier, Plus $20/mo, Team $25/mo, Enterprise custom

agents.name: Gemini
agents.description: Google's multimodal AI assistant with deep integration into Google Workspace, Search, and Android, capable of handling text, images, code, and long documents.
agents.pricing: Free tier, Advanced $19.99/mo (included with Google One AI Premium)

agents.name: Gemini Spark
agents.description: A 24/7 personal AI agent announced at Google I/O May 2026 that runs continuously in the background, managing Gmail, Google Calendar, and 30+ third-party tools via MCP connections. Designed to handle tasks proactively with user approval gates.
agents.pricing: Google AI Ultra subscription required (~$100/mo); US beta access for Ultra subscribers

agents.name: OpenClaw
agents.description: Open-source personal AI agent that runs locally, keeps context across conversations, and acts on the user's own machine, driven mainly through messaging platforms rather than a chat window. Shipped in 2025 as Clawdbot, renamed Moltbot over a trademark conflict, and settled on OpenClaw in January 2026 before passing 100,000 GitHub stars the month after.
agents.pricing: Free and open source; you pay only whatever model provider it calls

agents.name: Grok Bot
agents.description: Always-on agents that each get their own cloud computer, sign into a customer's existing tools, and finish multi-step jobs unsupervised, including inside apps and sites that expose no clean API or MCP integration. Work continues after the user closes the laptop, and the agent comes back when it needs approval rather than direction at every step.
agents.pricing: No standalone plan and no published per-bot fee. Beta access ships with SuperGrok Heavy (about $300/mo), Cursor Ultra ($200/mo), and Cursor Teams Premium ($120/user/mo), each including weekly usage with on-demand overage billed at model and token cost

agents.name: Claude
agents.description: A helpful AI assistant known for nuanced instruction-following, long-context understanding, and careful reasoning across writing, analysis, coding, and research tasks.
agents.pricing: Free tier, Pro $20/mo, Team $25/mo, Enterprise custom

agents.name: Midjourney
agents.description: A leading AI image generation tool that creates high-quality, artistic images from text prompts, known for its distinctive aesthetic style and photorealistic output.
agents.pricing: Basic $10/mo, Standard $30/mo, Pro $60/mo

agents.name: DALL-E 3
agents.description: OpenAI's image generation model integrated into ChatGPT and available via API, offering precise prompt adherence and the ability to render text within images.
agents.pricing: Included with ChatGPT Plus, API usage-based

agents.name: Suno
agents.description: An AI music generation platform that creates full songs with vocals, instruments, and lyrics from text prompts or custom lyrics input.
agents.pricing: Free tier, Pro $10/mo, Premier $30/mo

agents.name: LangChain
agents.description: An open-source framework for building LLM-powered applications with chains, agents, retrieval-augmented generation, and memory, supporting multiple model providers.
agents.pricing: Open source (LangSmith platform has paid tiers)

agents.name: CrewAI
agents.description: A framework for orchestrating role-playing AI agents that collaborate on complex tasks, allowing developers to define agent roles, goals, and delegation patterns.
agents.pricing: Open source, Enterprise cloud plans available

agents.name: AutoGen
agents.description: An open-source framework for building multi-agent conversational systems where multiple AI agents can collaborate, debate, and coordinate to solve tasks.
agents.pricing: Open source

agents.name: OpenAI Assistants API
agents.description: A platform API for building AI assistants with persistent threads, file retrieval, code interpretation, and function calling built into OpenAI's hosted infrastructure.
agents.pricing: Usage-based via OpenAI API

agents.name: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
agents.description: An open protocol that standardizes how AI applications connect to external data sources and tools, enabling plug-and-play integrations for any MCP-compatible client.
agents.pricing: Open source protocol
